content.comment_body: Hello, I'm using a [product_name] operator device to show the volume for a 70,000 litre tank. How can I get the display to show numbers up to 70,000 directly? I can easily display up to 7,000, but when I try to add an extra zero as text to extend the value, it doesn't appear aligned—it just looks like '7000 0' instead of a unified number. Could someone explain how to properly achieve this?
That isn't possible. The [product_name] system only supports integer values up to 326767 as the maximum.
Thanks. Is there a way to position a zero at the end of the displayed number so it appears as part of it and gives the impression of '70000'?
Unfortunately, that's also not possible with current formatting options.
Alright, thank you. I'll try to come up with another solution. At least I gave it a shot!

One possible workaround is to use an analog amplifier with Gain set to 7 and Offset set to 0, then set the display for two decimal places. This lets you show a range from 0 to 70.00, with a resolution of 70 litres. Hope this helps!

analysis.insight_summary: Users have difficulty displaying large numeric values on the [product_name] operator device due to system integer limits. Attempts to visually mimic higher numbers with text alignment or formatting are not supported, causing inconvenience. Suggested alternatives involve adjusting analog signals and decimal places, but these require users to accept less precise or differently formatted outputs.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want the [product_name] display to present large integers like 70,000 in an integrated and visually consistent way, similar to smaller values.
